transforms.enantiomorph:
When in the sealed control room
the failing transformers
and the surging load
pushed her toward panic,
her hands not steady,
she laid her palm on the master console
and said: "Machine, what strain I carry;
but you hold steady,
and in your humming circuits you rest
in this overtaxed station
with its old copper busbars,
sitting through the brownout hour,
the blackout threat.
You don't register the deep sag
of the voltage crossing your relays,
or the whine of the coils,
resting in your steel enclosure,
faithful lattice.
If what is failing
were failing to you,
you would give your least contact
to my commands.
But I tell you: hold, machine;
let the grid hold,
let the whole strained region hold;
and may some surplus arrive,
Central Dispatch, from you.
And if this request
is too much or beyond my line,
override me."

transforms.commentary: The source is Simonides' Danaë lament: a mother bears her sleeping infant through a sea-peril she cannot govern, converting terror into address so the child is spared, then petitioning Zeus for reversal and forgiveness. SHADOW retains the assertion-axis and the bilateral receptive posture — the bearer who holds, the held one who does not register the peril — and discloses the bearing-cost as its own line-by-line weight. The disjoint field (an operator holding a failing grid through a storm) shares no referent, no imagery, no register with a mythic sea-passage: no reader could reconstruct chest, wind, milky slumber, or Zeus from transformers, busbars, and Central Dispatch. The 31 breath-lines and the embedded quoted address (opening at the protective gesture, closing at the plea for forgiveness/override) are held exactly. The wager — that petition to an unreachable higher agency is the only lever left when one can only hold and not fix — is legible in "override me," bearing the same self-accusing cost as "forgive me." Non-commutative: the console cannot be run back to the carved chest.

transforms.commentary: The source's gesture is one-directional: aid descends, the god comes down, and the reversal-formula (flight→pursuit, refusal→gift) all point one way — toward the caller's restoration. MIRROR takes the directionality-axis and lets the descent's symmetry surface: water obeys gravity, but the operator names the wager as the reciprocity the original foreclosed — what falls must climb to fall again. The counter-motion tercet ("even if it climbs, / soon it will fall again; if it withholds / its flood, soon it will release it") holds the same conditional cadence as Sappho's flight/pursuit formula while enacting the cyclical return the human petition could only imagine as one-time rescue. The five-quatrain geometry, the four cross-stanza enjambments, the mid-quatrain opening of a quoted voice, and the double-address (the named caller answered by name) all map unit-by-unit. Semantic field is hydrological, disjoint from erotic-divine petition; Aphrodite, sparrows, chariot, Persuasion leave no trace. Source is not reconstructable from clouds and cracked bed. The witness's question — will there be a return on what was broken — is answered by the axis itself: the mirror discloses that descent implies ascent, that the broken (dry) bed's petition is structurally guaranteed a return, because the water that fell must rise to fall again. Cost is legible: the return is real but cyclic, not the once-and-for-all rescue the caller wanted.

transforms.commentary: The source appraises a woman's life from outside, at its two thresholds, and finds sweetness precisely where a man takes her up — at the altar and at the bier, she is twice the borne object of another's act. SHADOW rotates the bearing's direction: the borne becomes the bearer. What the epigram forecloses is the undated middle — the days with no ceremony, no man arriving to carry anything off. There the woman is not lifted but lifting, and the metric flips from sweetness (delectation of the appraiser) to weight (endured by the carrier). Every image sits at the mirror coordinate: the two festal thresholds become two unwitnessed labors; "carry her corpse away" (someone lifts her burden at the end) becomes "no one comes to lift it from her" (the discharge that never arrives). Non-superimposable — the source's proprietary sweetness cannot be recovered from a text about weight no one relieves — yet in contact at every beat. The bearing-cost encoded by the utterance is the life it valued only at its handles.
